A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the Plan2Align-to-TMPC rename and substantial revision. All 28 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v3, including appendices, figures, tables and equations, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original long-form response and machine-translation experiments, a Vanilla MPC ablation, and translation-metric validation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original response and translation results and adds program-synthesis results, additional baseline comparisons, and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The original rollout, buffer and regeneration loop largely survives the rename. However, v3 adds a substantive program-synthesis adaptation using unit-test rewards, failed-test feedback, debugging/diversification prompts and reuse of successful strategies (Appendix H.3). The exact buffer representation remains ambiguous because Appendix H also describes storing validated code snippets.

E1.justification: v3 adds MBPP program synthesis with 500 Python problems while retaining HH-RLHF and WMT’24 literary translation in the same three Chinese-source directions. It removes v2 Appendix H’s WMT24 general-translation and metrics-shared-task evaluations, including additional language pairs and simulated omission/over-translation scenarios.

E2.justification: RE-Control, GenARM and TPO become evaluated comparators in the retained translation and response experiments (v3 Table 1 and Figure 3); RE-Control was previously only discussed. Standalone Vanilla MPC rows disappear from those comparisons, although a related full-response refinement variant remains in v3’s zh→en iteration analysis.

E3.justification: v3 drops response coherence/diversity and translation CW-KIWI/d-BLEU metrics. It introduces unit-test-based MBPP evaluation with five planning iterations and two rollouts per iteration, plus buffer/segment-size, weaker-reward-model and injected-noise protocols. The reported HH-RLHF quality threshold changes from 3 to 4 (v2 G.1.1 versus v3 H.1.1); this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 5 and Table 3 add sensitivity to buffer/segment sizes, weaker and noisy rewards, and iteration counts. The earlier Vanilla MPC question is revisited through an iteration-wise degenerate-buffer comparison. Conversely, v2’s alignment sanity checks, MetricX error-sensitivity analysis and three scoring-failure case studies are removed.

E5.justification: Removing v2 Appendix H also removes Table 5’s score-distribution standard deviations and Figure 9’s Kendall correlation estimation. These were distribution/correlation statistics, not uncertainty across repeated model runs. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests for the principal comparisons.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial baseline, robustness and programming results: MBPP pass rates are 61% for TMPC, 50% for Best-of-35 and 48% for TPO. New translation results include TPO outperforming TMPC on zh→ru, 92.63 versus 91.53. Earlier headline COMET values, response rewards and GPT-4 win counts are retained up to rounding, while coherence/diversity, CW-KIWI/d-BLEU and metric-validation result entries disappear.

T1.justification: Beyond reformulating the retained trajectory-planning framework, v3 explicitly specifies deterministic text transitions, removes expectations from the objectives, and switches MPPI weighting from exp(-J/λ) to exp(J/λ) under a reward convention. Aggregation and buffer updates receive formal definitions. These are limited formal revisions; neither version supplies theorems or convergence proofs.

C1.justification: v2 principally claims efficient segment-based alignment for two long-form tasks. v3 adds a central claim that sequential decision making exposes a horizon-versus-dimensionality tradeoff, and presents hindsight subgoals as a general solution for tasks with and without natural boundaries, now including program synthesis.

C2.justification: v3 introduces substantive explanations involving horizon length, search dimensionality, test-driven code refinement and buffer-mediated robustness to imperfect rewards. It also discusses TPO failures, RE-Control training difficulties and hardware-dependent timing. v2’s detailed translation-metric failure interpretations disappear, while its limitation concerning the base model’s expressive capabilities remains in v3 Appendix B.

D1.justification: v3 adds programming prompts and settings, GenARM/RE-Control/TPO implementation descriptions, TPO call budgets and memory constraints, and the H200-versus-RTX-6000 timing disclosure. Its generic pseudocode omits v2’s explicit translation-finalization branch despite retaining the final-translation prompt. Release commitments also change from MIT-licensed settings/models/preference data to permissively licensed implementation and scripts upon publication; neither PDF establishes actual release.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions the work against both guided decoding and iterative textual refinement, adding discussion of GenARM and TPO and a horizon-reduction reference. Translation evaluation is now attributed to SEGALE. Several robotics examples and translation-metric validation references from v2 are removed, changing the research positioning beyond bibliographic formatting.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology and conclusion are extensively rewritten around TMPC and subgoals. v3 adds a Background section, changes the task ordering, reorganizes appendices, and introduces ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1, revises the method schematic, converts Figure 3’s response-results table into a reward bar chart, and adds programming, robustness and runtime plots. Table 1 replaces CW-KIWI columns with renamed alignment-ratio results previously in the appendix. Metric-validation displays disappear, while several prompt figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens comparisons with iterative refinement and adds useful programming and robustness evidence. However, it removes v2’s local translation-metric validation and introduces conflicting code-buffer descriptions. New evidence also contradicts claims: TPO beats TMPC on zh→ru in Table 1, and the claimed sensitivity below 0.1 conflicts with 4.595 versus 4.482 in Table 3. These gains and reliability problems leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
